---
title: "The widely applicable information criterion"
---

The [PSIS-LOO page](psis-loo.qmd) used full-posterior draws to approximate omitted-position posteriors. The [**widely applicable information criterion (WAIC)**](https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/waic.html) instead corrects fitted pointwise posterior predictive density using posterior variation. Both calculations require the same pointwise likelihood matrix, but their approximations differ.

## Fitted posterior predictive density

For observation $i$, the [**log pointwise predictive density (lppd)**](https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/waic.html) is

$$
\operatorname{lppd}_i
=
\log\left[
\frac{1}{S}
\sum_{s=1}^S
f(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})
\right].
$$

The average integrates the likelihood of $y_i$ over posterior uncertainty. But $y_i$ helped determine the posterior, so this remains a fitted predictive quantity. Summing gives

$$
\operatorname{lppd}=\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{lppd}_i.
$$

## The pointwise optimism correction

WAIC estimates effective flexibility from the posterior variance of each pointwise log likelihood:

$$
p_{\mathrm{waic},i}
=
\operatorname{Var}_s\left[
\log f(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})
\right],
$$

and

$$
p_{\mathrm{waic}}
=
\sum_{i=1}^Np_{\mathrm{waic},i}.
$$

The effective count depends on the fitted posterior, not merely on the number of regression coefficients. WAIC's expected log predictive density is

$$
\operatorname{elpd}_{\mathrm{waic}}
=
\operatorname{lppd}-p_{\mathrm{waic}}.
$$

Larger values are preferred. The deviance-scale quantity is

$$
\operatorname{WAIC}=-2\operatorname{elpd}_{\mathrm{waic}},
$$

for which smaller is preferred.

## WAIC and exact LOO for the Provo models

The code independently reloads the [Provo data](likelihood-ratio-tests.qmd#provo-corpus), reconstructs the fixed conjugate posteriors, and generates the same independent posterior draws used for PSIS. It computes WAIC both manually and with `loo::waic()`, then compares each pointwise WAIC contribution with exact LOO.

```{r}
#| label: provo-waic
#| message: false
#| warning: false

provo <- utils::read.csv(
  "data/provo/content-word-positions.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
provo$cloze_surprisal_bits <- -log2(provo$OrthoMatchModel)
y <- provo$mean_log_ffd

linear_fit <- lm(
  mean_log_ffd ~ cloze_surprisal_bits,
  data = provo
)
quadratic_fit <- lm(
  mean_log_ffd ~ cloze_surprisal_bits + I(cloze_surprisal_bits^2),
  data = provo
)
X_linear <- model.matrix(linear_fit)
X_quadratic <- model.matrix(quadratic_fit)

make_prior <- function(X) {
  log_bounds <- log(c(80, 800))
  log_span <- diff(log_bounds)
  expected_sigma2 <- (log_span / 4)^2
  list(
    b0 = c(mean(log_bounds), rep(0, ncol(X) - 1L)),
    V0 = diag(rep(log_span^2 / expected_sigma2, ncol(X))),
    a0 = 3,
    d0 = 2 * expected_sigma2
  )
}

nig_posterior <- function(X, y, prior) {
  V0_inverse <- solve(prior$V0)
  Vn <- solve(V0_inverse + crossprod(X))
  bn <- drop(Vn %*% (
    V0_inverse %*% prior$b0 + crossprod(X, y)
  ))
  an <- prior$a0 + length(y) / 2
  dn <- as.numeric(
    prior$d0 + 0.5 * (
      crossprod(y) +
        t(prior$b0) %*% V0_inverse %*% prior$b0 -
        t(bn) %*% solve(Vn) %*% bn
    )
  )
  list(Vn = Vn, bn = bn, an = an, dn = dn)
}

draw_nig <- function(posterior, draws, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  sigma2 <- 1 / rgamma(
    draws, shape = posterior$an, rate = posterior$dn
  )
  standard_normal <- matrix(
    rnorm(draws * length(posterior$bn)), nrow = draws
  )
  beta <- matrix(
    posterior$bn,
    nrow = draws,
    ncol = length(posterior$bn),
    byrow = TRUE
  ) + sweep(
    standard_normal %*% chol(posterior$Vn),
    1,
    sqrt(sigma2),
    "*"
  )
  list(beta = beta, sigma2 = sigma2)
}

log_likelihood_matrix <- function(X, y, draws) {
  mu <- draws$beta %*% t(X)
  standardized <- sweep(mu, 2, y, "-")
  standardized <- sweep(
    standardized, 1, sqrt(draws$sigma2), "/"
  )
  -0.5 * log(2 * pi) - 0.5 * log(draws$sigma2) -
    0.5 * standardized^2
}

exact_nig_loo <- function(X, y, prior) {
  n <- nrow(X)
  V0_inverse <- solve(prior$V0)
  full_xtx <- crossprod(X)
  full_xty <- crossprod(X, y)
  full_yty <- sum(y^2)
  log_density <- numeric(n)

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    xi <- matrix(X[i, ], nrow = 1L)
    yi <- y[i]
    Vn <- solve(V0_inverse + full_xtx - crossprod(xi))
    bn <- drop(Vn %*% (
      V0_inverse %*% prior$b0 + full_xty - drop(xi) * yi
    ))
    an <- prior$a0 + (n - 1L) / 2
    dn <- as.numeric(
      prior$d0 + 0.5 * (
        full_yty - yi^2 +
          t(prior$b0) %*% V0_inverse %*% prior$b0 -
          t(bn) %*% solve(Vn) %*% bn
      )
    )
    location <- drop(xi %*% bn)
    scale <- sqrt(
      (dn / an) * (1 + drop(xi %*% Vn %*% t(xi)))
    )
    degrees <- 2 * an
    log_density[i] <-
      dt((yi - location) / scale, df = degrees, log = TRUE) -
      log(scale)
  }
  log_density
}

stable_log_mean_exp <- function(values) {
  maximum <- max(values)
  maximum + log(mean(exp(values - maximum)))
}

manual_waic <- function(log_lik) {
  lppd <- apply(log_lik, 2, stable_log_mean_exp)
  p_waic <- apply(log_lik, 2, var)
  data.frame(
    lppd = lppd,
    p_waic = p_waic,
    elpd_waic = lppd - p_waic
  )
}

linear_prior <- make_prior(X_linear)
quadratic_prior <- make_prior(X_quadratic)
linear_posterior <- nig_posterior(X_linear, y, linear_prior)
quadratic_posterior <- nig_posterior(
  X_quadratic, y, quadratic_prior
)

posterior_draws <- 4000L
linear_draws <- draw_nig(
  linear_posterior, posterior_draws, seed = 20261104
)
quadratic_draws <- draw_nig(
  quadratic_posterior, posterior_draws, seed = 20261105
)
linear_log_lik <- log_likelihood_matrix(
  X_linear, y, linear_draws
)
quadratic_log_lik <- log_likelihood_matrix(
  X_quadratic, y, quadratic_draws
)

linear_pointwise <- manual_waic(linear_log_lik)
quadratic_pointwise <- manual_waic(quadratic_log_lik)
linear_waic <- loo::waic(linear_log_lik)
quadratic_waic <- loo::waic(quadratic_log_lik)

waic_summary <- data.frame(
  model = c("Linear", "Quadratic"),
  elpd_waic = c(
    linear_waic$estimates["elpd_waic", "Estimate"],
    quadratic_waic$estimates["elpd_waic", "Estimate"]
  ),
  p_waic = c(
    linear_waic$estimates["p_waic", "Estimate"],
    quadratic_waic$estimates["p_waic", "Estimate"]
  ),
  waic_deviance = c(
    linear_waic$estimates["waic", "Estimate"],
    quadratic_waic$estimates["waic", "Estimate"]
  )
)
stopifnot(max(abs(
  waic_summary$elpd_waic - c(
    sum(linear_pointwise$elpd_waic),
    sum(quadratic_pointwise$elpd_waic)
  )
)) < 1e-12)
waic_summary

linear_exact <- exact_nig_loo(X_linear, y, linear_prior)
quadratic_exact <- exact_nig_loo(
  X_quadratic, y, quadratic_prior
)
comparison_plot <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    surprisal = provo$cloze_surprisal_bits,
    model = "Linear",
    waic_minus_exact = linear_pointwise$elpd_waic - linear_exact
  ),
  data.frame(
    surprisal = provo$cloze_surprisal_bits,
    model = "Quadratic",
    waic_minus_exact =
      quadratic_pointwise$elpd_waic - quadratic_exact
  )
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  comparison_plot,
  ggplot2::aes(surprisal, waic_minus_exact)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0, color = "grey55", linewidth = 0.45
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.3, color = "grey25") + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ model) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Modeled cloze surprisal (bits)",
    y = "Pointwise WAIC minus exact LOO contribution"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11)
```

WAIC gives ELPD `r sprintf("%.3f", waic_summary$elpd_waic[waic_summary$model == "Linear"])` with $p_{\mathrm{waic}} = `r sprintf("%.3f", waic_summary$p_waic[waic_summary$model == "Linear"])`$ for the linear model. The quadratic values are `r sprintf("%.3f", waic_summary$elpd_waic[waic_summary$model == "Quadratic"])` and $p_{\mathrm{waic}} = `r sprintf("%.3f", waic_summary$p_waic[waic_summary$model == "Quadratic"])`$. The manual pointwise implementation and `loo::waic()` agree to the asserted numerical tolerance.

The figure shows the approximation rather than another abstract score: every point is one Provo position's WAIC contribution minus its exact LOO contribution. Most differences cluster near zero, but the display preserves their relation to modeled cloze surprisal.

## What the correction does not change

WAIC is tied to the unit represented by one likelihood column. Here that unit is an aggregated content-word position. The correction does not create prediction for a wholly new reader, word type, or passage. Other positions from the same passage remain part of the fitted posterior used to calculate each contribution.

Large posterior variance in a pointwise log likelihood can warn that WAIC is unreliable for that position. The warning concerns the approximation; it does not license discarding a linguistically surprising point. PSIS-LOO is often easier to diagnose because Pareto $k$ targets its importance-sampling approximation directly.

Finally, WAIC ranks compatible candidate models. It does not establish that the preferred predictor causes the reading response or explains the linguistic process that produced it.

## Checking the correction

1. Why is lppd a fitted rather than omitted-data quantity?
2. Which posterior quantity supplies WAIC's optimism correction?
3. Why can $p_{\mathrm{waic}}$ differ from a coefficient count?
4. What is the empirical unit of one point in the final figure?

WAIC subtracts a posterior-variance correction from fitted pointwise predictive density. The [previous page](psis-loo.qmd) approximated omitted-position posteriors with importance sampling. Return to the [module overview](index.qmd) to place both approximations within the full model-evaluation sequence.
